  - **VIX above 20 and rising: ARMED.** VIX is 19.41 (2026-10-26, yfinance, −0.21%) and needs +3.0%. It is slightly further away than before.
  - **VXN at 25 or more with TQQQ more than 20% below its 4-week high: FIRED on both legs.** VXN is 28.30. TQQQ is 22.3% below the $85.32 high.

  - **Bearish trigger "TQQQ close under the 4-week low": ARMED, not fired.** The 4-week low moved down from $65.61 to $65.37, so a lower low was set. The close of 66.29 is 1.4% above it. The data does not say whether the low is a close or an intraday print.
  - **Neutralizer (Brent below $100 and 10Y under 5.10%): half met.** The 10Y leg is met at 4.988%. Brent is $110.12 (2026-10-26) and needs −9.2%.
- Notable lens flips: Macro −1 → −2, because credit is now widening. All other lenses are unchanged. Positioning stays at 0 because the put/call reading is not available this run. Net −1.

Stage 5 (risk-off) holds. TQQQ is stuck in a downturn with high volatility, and credit has started to widen. VIX is still under 20, and the 10Y is no longer rising toward the 5.25% danger line. Confidence is **Medium**.

## Diverging Signals
- **Oversold vs risk-off.** TQQQ RSI is 22.4, which is deeper than the 27.5 of the previous read. Normally that supports a bounce. But the structure is DOWNTURN, the news daemon is in SHOCK, and there has been no green day. An oversold reading can stay oversold in a falling market.
- **Credit is widening, but VIX is under 20.** HY OAS rose to 3.40% while VIX is 19.41. Credit stress without a VIX spike is the least-confirmed way into Stage 5. If VIX closes above 20 the picture agrees with itself. If credit reverses, the Stage 5 call weakens.
- **Yields moved two ways.** The 2Y fell 16bp (4.81% → 4.65%) while the 10Y rose to 4.988%. The 2Y drop could mean the market expects the Fed to cut. It could also be a flight to safety. The data here cannot tell which.
- **Brent is falling, but is still high.** Brent is −5.65% on the day, yet it is $110.12, above the $100 neutralizer. One lower print does not change the energy-cost backdrop.

## TQQQ Read
- Momentum: RSI 22.4 is oversold, down from 27.5 in the previous read. Oversold usually means rich premium and a mean-reversion tailwind, but only once selling stabilizes. Two red days and no green day do not show that yet.
- Market structure: **DOWNTURN.** Spot is 22.3% below the 4-week high of $85.32 (the test is more than 20%, line $68.26) and VXN is 28.30 (the test is 25 or more). Both legs are met. Spot is only 1.4% above the 4-week low, so this is not a rally structure (RALLY would need about $84.98).
- Trend: Below the 50DMA ($74.02) by 10.44%, and above the 200DMA (~$64.99) by only 2.0%. The 200DMA is the last major trend line, and it sits 2.0% below spot. Spot is 24.43% under the 52-week high.
- Volatility & premium environment: VXN is 28.30 (−1.46%), off the spike but still far above the 25 line. VVIX 109.70 and SKEW 151.80 remain high, so protection is expensive. MOVE is easing at 103.31. Premium should be fat, and swings will also be big, since TQQQ moves about 3× NDX. The IV/HV check (options price vs. realized movement) is unavailable this run.
- Put-selling context: HOSTILE. Premium is rich and RSI is deeply oversold. Against that, the structure is DOWNTURN, spot sits 1.4% above the 4-week low and 2.0% above the 200DMA, HY credit is widening, the news daemon is in SHOCK, and an FOMC decision lands in two sessions. Gap risk is high, and the oversold bounce is unconfirmed. Context only — no strikes, expiries or sizes.
